title: Add code-health check, status table, and design-review cadence
summary: Add crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs measuring per-file production lines, longest function, 7-day landing churn, failure citations, and test run time. Show it in athena status with thresholds, queue one structural-pass request per breaching file unless one is open, run it after each landing, and queue the design review at high priority every 10 landings. The audience is Sri and the verifier, who need breaches caught without being pointed out.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-based unit tests for the measures, queue dedup, and the cadence, with clippy and fmt clean.
Criteria check that the breach produces exactly one queued request and the status table renders, not that the code exists.
Reuse an existing parser dependency for function length if one is present, and record the call in decisions.md.
Behavior criteria are checkable with cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One module plus thin hooks into status, display and the landing path.
The check runs automatically after each landing and queues requests by code, not by prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: Athena watches its own code health and queues structural passes itself, so Sri need not point problems out.

Production lines exclude #[cfg(test)] modules; function length is measured with a Rust parser (syn, if already a dependency) or a simple brace-matching scan, and the choice is recorded in decisions.md.
Landings per file come from landing records in the state dir; failures cited come from job failure and rejection records that name the file.
Thresholds are the example values from the request, held as constants or in config, with no change to athena.toml.
The design-review role from job 20261017-205558-dn2e already exists; this job only adds a landing-count trigger that queues it at high priority every 10 landings, separate from the steward tick.
Test suite run time is measured when the check runs, or read from the last recorded run, and not by running cargo test inside the check on every landing; the producer picks one and notes it.
The 'run after every landing' hook goes in the existing post-landing path, likely in gh.rs or land.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a code_health test with fixture source files and landing records asserts per-file production line count (excluding #[cfg(test)] modules), longest function length, landings in last 7 days, and failure/rejection citations; a breach of each threshold (file >2000 lines, function >200 lines, >1500 lines with >=5 landings in a week) is reported.

Run cargo test: on a breach exactly one structural-pass request is queued for that file, citing the measured numbers; running the check again, or with an open structural-pass request for that file, queues none.
Run cargo test: the design-review request is queued at high priority at the 10th landed job since the last review and not at the 9th, on its own cadence independent of the steward's.
Run cargo test: the check runs after every landing (a test of the post-landing path shows it invoked), and the test suite run time is recorded in the report.
Run cargo test: the athena status output (rendered in a test) contains the code-health table with each file's lines, longest function, weekly landings, citations, thresholds, and test run time.
cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are clean and cargo test passes.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry and docs/decisions.md records the thresholds, the buy-versus-build call on measuring function length, and the 10-landing cadence.

out_of_scope: Changing the design-review role's prompt or its output format
Changing the steward's cadence or behavior
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: a new module, status and display integration, a post-landing hook and three behavior tests across several files. Pass probability is slightly lower because the scope is wide.
urgent_reason: Without this check, oversized files and churn are found by Sri pointing them out, which costs extra requests and redo work; the check queues structural passes automatically.
